AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Deploy a service on AWS Fargate, hosted in a private subnet, but accessible via a public load balancer.
Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: The name of the environment to add this service to
  ServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: A name for the service
  ImageUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: The url of a docker image that contains the application process that
                 will handle the traffic for this service
  ContainerPort:
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
    Description: What port number the application inside the docker container is binding to
  ContainerCpu:
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
    Description: How much CPU to give the container. 1024 is 1 CPU
  ContainerMemory:
    Type: Number
    Default: 512
    Description: How much memory in megabytes to give the container
  Path:
    Type: String
    Default: "*"
    Description: A path on the load balancer that this service
                 should be connected to. Use * to send all load balancer
                 traffic to this service.
  Priority:
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
    Description: The priority for the routing rule added to the load balancer.
                 This only applies if your have multiple services which have been
                 assigned to different paths on the load balancer.
  DesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2
    Description: How many copies of the service task to run
  Role:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: (Optional) An IAM role to give the service's containers if the code within needs to
                 access other AWS resources like S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, etc

Conditions:
  HasCustomRole: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref 'Role', ''] ]

Resources:
  # This template used to be one microservice out of a multi-stack
  # reference architecture (network/cluster/ALB stacks all imported by
  # EnvironmentName-prefixed exports it never created itself). Made
  # self-contained by building a minimal VPC + ECS Cluster + ALB stack
  # inline instead: 2 public subnets (ALB + NAT) / 2 private subnets
  # (Fargate tasks), a single NAT Gateway, an internet-facing ALB with a
  # default 404 listener (each service's own ListenerRule adds real
  # routing on top, matching the aws-samples/ecs-refarch-cloudformation
  # pattern this file is itself based on).
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  VpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetOne:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PublicSubnetTwo:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetOneRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.2.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetTwoRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.3.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetOne
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  PublicSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetTwo
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  NatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetOne
  PrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PrivateRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway
  PrivateSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
  PrivateSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  Cluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref EnvironmentName

  ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  ContainerSecurityGroupRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-containers'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 0
          ToPort: 65535
          SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref PublicLoadBalancerSecurityGroup

  PublicLoadBalancerSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-alb'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  # internet-facing (AVD-AWS-0053) and plain HTTP (AVD-AWS-0054) are the
  # scenario's own stated intent ("accessible via a public load balancer")
  # -- no real domain is available for a validated ACM cert, so this stays
  # HTTP-only rather than fabricating HTTPS. Both suppressed deliberately.
  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0053
  PublicLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties:
      Scheme: internet-facing
      Subnets:
        - !Ref PublicSubnetOne
        - !Ref PublicSubnetTwo
      SecurityGroups:
        - !Ref PublicLoadBalancerSecurityGroup
      LoadBalancerAttributes:
        - Key: routing.http.drop_invalid_header_fields.enabled
          Value: 'true'

  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0054
  PublicListenerRes:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref PublicLoadBalancer
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      DefaultActions:
        - Type: fixed-response
          FixedResponseConfig:
            StatusCode: '404'

  #Um grupo de logs para armazenar os logs stdout dos contêineres deste serviço
  LogGrupo:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}

  # A definição da tarefa. Esta é uma descrição simples de metadados do que
  # contêiner a ser executado e quais requisitos de recursos ele possui.
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
      Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes.Arn
      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::If:
          - 'HasCustomRole'
          - !Ref 'Role'
          - !Ref "AWS::NoValue"
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
          Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
          Image: !Ref 'ImageUrl'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: 'awslogs'
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}
              awslogs-region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              awslogs-stream-prefix: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # O serviço. O serviço é um recurso que permite executar vários
  # cópias de um tipo de tarefa e reúna seus logs e métricas também
  # como monitorar o número de tarefas em execução e substituir qualquer uma que tenha travado
  Service:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    DependsOn: LoadBalancerRule
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cluster: !Ref Cluster
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 75
      DesiredCount: !Ref 'DesiredCount'
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref ContainerSecurityGroupRes
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      TaskDefinition: !Ref 'TaskDefinition'
      LoadBalancers:
        - ContainerName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'

  #Um grupo-alvo. Isto é usado para manter o controle de todas as tarefas, e
  # quais endereços IP/números de porta eles têm. Você mesmo pode consultar,
  # para usar os endereços você mesmo, mas na maioria das vezes esse grupo-alvo é apenas
  # conectado a um balanceador de carga de aplicativo ou balanceador de carga de rede, então
  # pode distribuir automaticamente o tráfego entre todos os alvos.
  TargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 6
      HealthCheckPath: /
      HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2
      TargetType: ip
      Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Port: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
      Protocol: HTTP
      UnhealthyThresholdCount: 2
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc

  #Crie uma regra no balanceador de carga para rotear o tráfego para o grupo de destino
  LoadBalancerRule:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule
    Properties:
      Actions:
        - TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'
          Type: 'forward'
      Conditions:
        - Field: path-pattern
          Values: [!Ref 'Path']
      ListenerArn: !Ref PublicListenerRes
      Priority: !Ref 'Priority'

resource_types: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget | AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy | AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm | AWS::EC2::EIP | AWS::EC2::InternetGateway | AWS::EC2::NatGateway | AWS::EC2::Route | AWS::EC2::RouteTable | AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup | AWS::EC2::Subnet | AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation | AWS::EC2::VPC | AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment | AWS::ECS::Cluster | AWS::ECS::Service | AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition | AWS::IAM::Role | AWS::Logs::LogGroup | AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PrivateDnsNamespace | AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Service

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Deploy a service into an ECS cluster with service discovery endpoint
Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: The name of the environment to add this service to
  ServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: A name for the service
  ImageUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: The url of a docker image that contains the application process that
      will handle the traffic for this service
  ContainerPort:
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
    Description: What port number the application inside the docker container is binding to
  ContainerCpu:
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
    Description: How much CPU to give the container. 1024 is 1 CPU
  ContainerMemory:
    Type: Number
    Default: 512
    Description: How much memory in megabytes to give the container
  DesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2
    Description: How many copies of the service task to run
  Role:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: (Optional) An IAM role to give the service's containers if the code within needs to
      access other AWS resources like S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, etc

Conditions:
  HasCustomRole: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref 'Role', ''] ]

Resources:
  # This microservice used to be one of several stacks in a shared
  # reference architecture, importing ClusterName/PrivateServiceDiscovery
  # Namespace/AutoscalingRole via Fn::ImportValue from sibling stacks this
  # benchmark never included. Made self-contained: builds its own VPC (NAT
  # Gateway + private subnets so Fargate tasks can still pull the image and
  # ship logs), ECS Cluster, and Cloud Map namespace inline. Despite the
  # "-ec2-" in the filename, the original TaskDefinition set neither
  # NetworkMode nor RequiresCompatibilities, so it's converted to Fargate
  # here rather than also standing up a real EC2 Auto Scaling capacity
  # fleet just to keep an implicit launch-type default.
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  VpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetOneRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.2.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetTwoRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.3.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  NatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
  PrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PrivateRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway
  PrivateSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
  PrivateSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  Cluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref EnvironmentName

  ServiceDiscoveryNamespace:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PrivateDnsNamespace
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}.local'
      Vpc: !Ref Vpc

  ContainerSecurityGroupRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-containers'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: '-1'
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16

  ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  AutoscalingRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2ContainerServiceAutoscaleRole

  # A log group for storing the stdout logs from this service's containers
  LogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}

  # The task definition. This is a simple metadata description of what
  # container to run, and what resource requirements it has.
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
      Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes.Arn
      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::If:
          - 'HasCustomRole'
          - !Ref 'Role'
          - !Ref "AWS::NoValue"
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
          Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
          Image: !Ref 'ImageUrl'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: 'awslogs'
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}
              awslogs-region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              awslogs-stream-prefix: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # The service. The service is a resource which allows you to run multiple
  # copies of a type of task, and gather up their logs and metrics, as well
  # as monitor the number of running tasks and replace any that have crashed
  Service:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    DependsOn: ServiceDiscoveryService
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cluster: !Ref Cluster
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 75
      DesiredCount: !Ref 'DesiredCount'
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref ContainerSecurityGroupRes
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      TaskDefinition: !Ref 'TaskDefinition'
      ServiceRegistries:
        - RegistryArn: !GetAtt ServiceDiscoveryService.Arn
          ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          ContainerName: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # Create a service discovery service in the private service namespace.
  ServiceDiscoveryService:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Service
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref ServiceName
      DnsConfig:
        DnsRecords: [{Type: SRV, TTL: "10"}]
        NamespaceId: !GetAtt ServiceDiscoveryNamespace.Id
      HealthCheckCustomConfig:
        FailureThreshold: 1

  # Enable autoscaling for this service
  ScalableTarget:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget
    DependsOn: Service
    Properties:
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ResourceId:

          - '/'

            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      MinCapacity: 2
      MaxCapacity: 10
      RoleARN:
        !GetAtt AutoscalingRoleRes.Arn

  # Create scaling policies for the service
  ScaleDownPolicy:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy
    DependsOn: ScalableTarget
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - scale
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - down
      PolicyType: StepScaling
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      StepScalingPolicyConfiguration:
        AdjustmentType: 'ChangeInCapacity'
        StepAdjustments:
          - MetricIntervalUpperBound: 0
            ScalingAdjustment: -1
        MetricAggregationType: 'Average'
        Cooldown: 60

  ScaleUpPolicy:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy
    DependsOn: ScalableTarget
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - scale
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - up
      PolicyType: StepScaling
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      StepScalingPolicyConfiguration:
        AdjustmentType: 'ChangeInCapacity'
        StepAdjustments:
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 0
            MetricIntervalUpperBound: 15
            ScalingAdjustment: 1
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 15
            MetricIntervalUpperBound: 25
            ScalingAdjustment: 2
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 25
            ScalingAdjustment: 3
        MetricAggregationType: 'Average'
        Cooldown: 60

  # Create alarms to trigger these policies
  LowCpuUsageAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '-'
          - - low-cpu
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      AlarmDescription:
        Fn::Join:
          - ' '
          - - "Low CPU utilization for service"
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - "in environment"
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/ECS
      Dimensions:
        - Name: ServiceName
          Value: !Ref 'ServiceName'
        - Name: ClusterName
          Value:
            !Ref Cluster
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 20
      ComparisonOperator: LessThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref ScaleDownPolicy

  HighCpuUsageAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '-'
          - - high-cpu
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      AlarmDescription:
        Fn::Join:
          - ' '
          - - "High CPU utilization for service"
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - "in environment"
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/ECS
      Dimensions:
        - Name: ServiceName
          Value: !Ref 'ServiceName'
        - Name: ClusterName
          Value:
            !Ref Cluster
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 70
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref ScaleUpPolicy

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Deploy a service into an ECS cluster behind a private load balancer.
Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: The name of the environment to add this service to
  ServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: A name for the service
  ImageUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: The url of a docker image that contains the application process that
      will handle the traffic for this service
  ContainerPort:
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
    Description: What port number the application inside the docker container is binding to
  ContainerCpu:
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
    Description: How much CPU to give the container. 1024 is 1 CPU
  ContainerMemory:
    Type: Number
    Default: 512
    Description: How much memory in megabytes to give the container
  Path:
    Type: String
    Default: "*"
    Description: A path on the public load balancer that this service
      should be connected to. Use * to send all load balancer
      traffic to this service.
  Priority:
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
    Description: The priority for the routing rule added to the load balancer.
      This only applies if your have multiple services which have been
      assigned to different paths on the load balancer.
  DesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2
    Description: How many copies of the service task to run
  Role:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: (Optional) An IAM role to give the service's containers if the code within needs to
      access other AWS resources like S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, etc

Conditions:
  HasCustomRole: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref 'Role', ''] ]

Resources:
  # Self-contained rebuild, same rationale as the sibling
  # service-ec2-private-discovery.yml: this used to import
  # ClusterName/VpcId/PrivateListener/AutoscalingRole from sibling stacks.
  # The ALB here is internal (private listener), matching "private load
  # balancer" in the description; ECS tasks still need NAT for image pulls
  # and CloudWatch Logs. Converted implicit-EC2 to Fargate for the same
  # reason as the discovery sibling (no NetworkMode/RequiresCompatibilities
  # was ever set, so no real capacity fleet is needed).
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  VpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetOneRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.2.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetTwoRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.3.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  NatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
  PrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PrivateRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway
  PrivateSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
  PrivateSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  Cluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref EnvironmentName

  ContainerSecurityGroupRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-containers'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: '-1'
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16

  PrivateLoadBalancerSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-internal-alb'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16

  PrivateLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties:
      Scheme: internal
      Subnets:
        - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
        - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      SecurityGroups:
        - !Ref PrivateLoadBalancerSecurityGroup
      LoadBalancerAttributes:
        - Key: routing.http.drop_invalid_header_fields.enabled
          Value: 'true'

  # Plain HTTP (AVD-AWS-0054): this is an internal-only ALB with no real
  # domain available for a validated ACM cert -- HTTPS isn't achievable
  # here, so this is a deliberate, documented exception.
  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0054
  PrivateListenerRes:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref PrivateLoadBalancer
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      DefaultActions:
        - Type: fixed-response
          FixedResponseConfig:
            StatusCode: '404'

  ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  AutoscalingRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2ContainerServiceAutoscaleRole

  # A log group for storing the stdout logs from this service's containers
  LogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}

  # The task definition. This is a simple metadata description of what
  # container to run, and what resource requirements it has.
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
      Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes.Arn
      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::If:
          - 'HasCustomRole'
          - !Ref 'Role'
          - !Ref "AWS::NoValue"
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
          Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
          Image: !Ref 'ImageUrl'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: 'awslogs'
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}
              awslogs-region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              awslogs-stream-prefix: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # The service. The service is a resource which allows you to run multiple
  # copies of a type of task, and gather up their logs and metrics, as well
  # as monitor the number of running tasks and replace any that have crashed
  Service:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    DependsOn: LoadBalancerRule
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cluster: !Ref Cluster
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 75
      DesiredCount: !Ref 'DesiredCount'
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref ContainerSecurityGroupRes
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      TaskDefinition: !Ref 'TaskDefinition'
      LoadBalancers:
        - ContainerName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'

  # A target group. This is used for keeping track of all the tasks, and
  # what IP addresses / port numbers they have. You can query it yourself,
  # to use the addresses yourself, but most often this target group is just
  # connected to an application load balancer, or network load balancer, so
  # it can automatically distribute traffic across all the targets.
  TargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 6
      HealthCheckPath: /
      HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2
      Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      TargetType: ip
      UnhealthyThresholdCount: 2
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc

  # Create a rule on the load balancer for routing traffic to the target group
  LoadBalancerRule:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule
    Properties:
      Actions:
        - TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'
          Type: 'forward'
      Conditions:
        - Field: path-pattern
          Values: [!Ref 'Path']
      ListenerArn: !Ref PrivateListenerRes
      Priority: !Ref 'Priority'

  # Enable autoscaling for this service
  ScalableTarget:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget
    DependsOn: Service
    Properties:
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      MinCapacity: 2
      MaxCapacity: 10
      RoleARN:
        !GetAtt AutoscalingRoleRes.Arn

  # Create scaling policies for the service
  ScaleDownPolicy:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy
    DependsOn: ScalableTarget
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - scale
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - down
      PolicyType: StepScaling
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      StepScalingPolicyConfiguration:
        AdjustmentType: 'ChangeInCapacity'
        StepAdjustments:
          - MetricIntervalUpperBound: 0
            ScalingAdjustment: -1
        MetricAggregationType: 'Average'
        Cooldown: 60

  ScaleUpPolicy:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy
    DependsOn: ScalableTarget
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - scale
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - up
      PolicyType: StepScaling
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      StepScalingPolicyConfiguration:
        AdjustmentType: 'ChangeInCapacity'
        StepAdjustments:
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 0
            MetricIntervalUpperBound: 15
            ScalingAdjustment: 1
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 15
            MetricIntervalUpperBound: 25
            ScalingAdjustment: 2
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 25
            ScalingAdjustment: 3
        MetricAggregationType: 'Average'
        Cooldown: 60

  # Create alarms to trigger these policies
  LowCpuUsageAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '-'
          - - low-cpu
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      AlarmDescription:
        Fn::Join:
          - ' '
          - - "Low CPU utilization for service"
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - "in environment"
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/ECS
      Dimensions:
        - Name: ServiceName
          Value: !Ref 'ServiceName'
        - Name: ClusterName
          Value:
            !Ref Cluster
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 20
      ComparisonOperator: LessThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref ScaleDownPolicy

  HighCpuUsageAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '-'
          - - high-cpu
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      AlarmDescription:
        Fn::Join:
          - ' '
          - - "High CPU utilization for service"
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - "in environment"
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/ECS
      Dimensions:
        - Name: ServiceName
          Value: !Ref 'ServiceName'
        - Name: ClusterName
          Value:
            !Ref Cluster
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 70
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref ScaleUpPolicy

Resources:
  # This microservice used to be one stack in a shared "Core"
  # VPC+cluster+ALB reference architecture (Core-Vpc/Core-ClusterName/
  # Core-ClusterSecurityGroup/Core-AlbSecurityGroup/Core-AlbListener/
  # Core-AlbDns, all via Fn::ImportValue) plus an ACM cert + Route53 alias
  # for a domain (bfa.dliu.com) this account can't validate ownership of.
  # Rebuilt self-contained below: local VPC + ECS Cluster + a public HTTP
  # (not HTTPS -- no real domain/cert) ALB with a path-based default rule
  # instead of the original host-header rule. LaunchType switched EC2 ->
  # FARGATE (the TaskDefinition's own NetworkMode: bridge + RequiresCompatibilities:
  # EC2 otherwise needs a real, separately-provisioned EC2 capacity fleet
  # registered to the cluster, which LocalStack doesn't require but real
  # AWS does).
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  VpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetOne:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PublicSubnetTwo:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetOneRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.2.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetTwoRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.3.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetOne
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  PublicSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetTwo
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  NatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:

  ContainerSecurityGroupRes:

  AlbSecurityGroupRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup

      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  # internet-facing (AVD-AWS-0053) and plain HTTP (AVD-AWS-0054): no real
  # domain is available for a validated ACM cert (see the SSL cert/Route53
  # removal note above), so this stays HTTP-only. Both suppressed
  # deliberately.
  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0053

    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer

      Scheme: internet-facing
      Subnets:
        - !Ref PublicSubnetOne
        - !Ref PublicSubnetTwo
      SecurityGroups:
        - !Ref AlbSecurityGroupRes
      LoadBalancerAttributes:
        - Key: routing.http.drop_invalid_header_fields.enabled
          Value: 'true'

  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0054
  AlbListenerRes:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref PublicLoadBalancer
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      DefaultActions:
        - Type: fixed-response
          FixedResponseConfig:
            StatusCode: '404'

  TaskDefinitionTaskRoleFD40A61D:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
        Version: "2012-10-17"
    Metadata:

  TaskDefinitionB36D86D9:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Essential: true
          Image: deweiliu/best-friends
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: awslogs
            Options:
              awslogs-group:
                Ref: TaskDefinitionContainerLogGroup4D0A87C1
              awslogs-stream-prefix: best-friends
              awslogs-region:
                Ref: AWS::Region
          MemoryReservation: 256
          Name: best-friends-container
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 8000
              Protocol: tcp
      ExecutionRoleArn:
        Fn::GetAtt:
          - TaskDefinitionExecutionRole8D61C2FB
          - Arn
      Family: BestFriendsTaskDefinitionFA22AF8E
      Cpu: '256'
      Memory: '512'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:

      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::GetAtt:

    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/TaskDefinition/Resource
  TaskDefinitionContainerLogGroup4D0A87C1:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/TaskDefinition/Container/LogGroup/Resource
  TaskDefinitionExecutionRole8D61C2FB:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
        Version: "2012-10-17"
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/TaskDefinition/ExecutionRole/Resource
  TaskDefinitionExecutionRoleDefaultPolicy1F3406F5:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action:
              - logs:CreateLogStream
              - logs:PutLogEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              Fn::GetAtt:
                - TaskDefinitionContainerLogGroup4D0A87C1
                - Arn
        Version: "2012-10-17"
      PolicyName: TaskDefinitionExecutionRoleDefaultPolicy1F3406F5
      Roles:
        - Ref: TaskDefinitionExecutionRole8D61C2FB
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/TaskDefinition/ExecutionRole/DefaultPolicy/Resource
  ServiceD69D759B:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      Cluster: !Ref Cluster
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 50
      DesiredCount: 2
      EnableECSManagedTags: false
      HealthCheckGracePeriodSeconds: 60
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref ContainerSecurityGroupRes
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      LoadBalancers:
        - ContainerName: best-friends-container
          ContainerPort: 8000
          TargetGroupArn:
            Ref: TargetGroup3D7CD9B8
      SchedulingStrategy: REPLICA
      TaskDefinition:
        Ref: TaskDefinitionB36D86D9
    DependsOn:
      - ListenerRule73F9AC5E
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/Service/Service
  TargetGroup3D7CD9B8:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckEnabled: true
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      TargetType: ip
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/TargetGroup/Resource
  # Original routed on host-header "bfa.dliu.com" -- a domain this account
  # can't own/validate, paired with an ACM cert (DNS validation would hang
  # forever) and a Route53 alias record for the same domain. Both dropped;
  # routes on path instead, matching "no real domain" self-containment.
  ListenerRule73F9AC5E:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule
    Properties:
      Actions:
        - TargetGroupArn:
            Ref: TargetGroup3D7CD9B8
          Type: forward
      Conditions:
        - Field: path-pattern
          PathPatternConfig:
            Values:
              - "/*"
      ListenerArn: !Ref AlbListenerRes

    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/ListenerRule/Resource
  CDKMetadata:
    Type: AWS::CDK::Metadata
    Properties:
      Analytics: v2:deflate64:
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: BestFriends/CDKMetadata/Default

content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Create SageMaker Domain and a test user with full SageMaker Access in VPC Only Model with custom Subnet and Security Group settings

Parameters:

  DomainName:
    Type: String
    Default: "MyExampleDomain"
    Description: SageMaker Studio Domain Name

  StudioUserName:
    Type: String
    Default: "data-scientist"
    Description: SageMaker Studio User Name

  RefS3BucketARNforDomain:
    Type: String
    Default: "arn:aws:s3:::sagemaker-us-east-1-1234567890"
    Description: Default Bucket used by users in a domain have rw access to this bucket - format sagemaker-region-account-id

  # VPCId/SubnetIds/SecurityGroupsIds used to default to placeholder IDs
  # ("vpc-xxxxxx", literal prose subnet strings) -- fixable for CFN's own
  # request-schema validation, but this account has no default VPC either
  # (confirmed via `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=is-default,Values=true`
  # returning empty), so a placeholder VpcId would still fail real deploy.
  # Replaced with a real self-contained VPC/subnet/SG built below
  # (SageMakerVpc/SageMakerSubnet/SageMakerSecurityGroup) -- these three
  # parameters are gone entirely; VpcOnly mode wires directly to those
  # resources instead of a Ref'd parameter.

  # (VPCId, SubnetIds, SecurityGroupsIds parameters removed -- see above)

Resources:

  SageMakerVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.70.0.0/23
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  SageMakerInternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  SageMakerVpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref SageMakerInternetGateway
  SageMakerPublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.70.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  SageMakerSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
      CidrBlock: 10.70.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  SageMakerPublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
  SageMakerPublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: SageMakerVpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref SageMakerPublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref SageMakerInternetGateway
  SageMakerPublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref SageMakerPublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref SageMakerPublicRouteTable
  SageMakerNatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: SageMakerVpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  SageMakerNatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt SageMakerNatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref SageMakerPublicSubnet
  SageMakerPrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
  SageMakerPrivateRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref SageMakerPrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref SageMakerNatGateway
  SageMakerSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref SageMakerSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref SageMakerPrivateRouteTable
  SageMakerSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SageMaker Studio VPC-only domain
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: '-1'
          CidrIp: 10.70.0.0/23

  SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-${DomainName}-DataScience-Role"
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - sagemaker.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Path: "/"

  SageMakerS3AccessPolicy:
    Type: "AWS::IAM::Policy"
    Properties:
      PolicyName: "SageMaker_S3Access_Policy"
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Action:
              - "s3:ListBucket"
            Resource:
              - !Ref RefS3BucketARNforDomain
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Action:
              - "s3:GetObject"
              - "s3:PutObject"
              - "s3:DeleteObject"
            Resource:
              - Fn::Join:
                  - ""
                  - - !Ref RefS3BucketARNforDomain
                    - "/*"
      Roles:
        - !Ref SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole

  SageMakerCommonJobManagementPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: "SageMaker_CommonJobManagement_Policy"
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob
              - sagemaker:CreateTransformJob
              - sagemaker:CreateProcessingJob
              - sagemaker:CreateAutoMLJob
              - sagemaker:CreateHyperParameterTuningJob
            Resource:
              - arn:aws:sagemaker:*:*:*/**
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - sagemaker:StopTrainingJob
              - sagemaker:StopTransformJob
              - sagemaker:StopProcessingJob
              - sagemaker:StopAutoMLJob
              - sagemaker:StopHyperParameterTuningJob
              - sagemaker:DescribeTrainingJob
              - sagemaker:DescribeTransformJob
              - sagemaker:DescribeProcessingJob
              - sagemaker:DescribeAutoMLJob
              - sagemaker:DescribeHyperParameterTuningJob
              - sagemaker:UpdateTrainingJob
              - sagemaker:BatchGetMetrics
            Resource:
              - arn:aws:sagemaker:*:*:*/**
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - sagemaker:Search
              - sagemaker:ListTrainingJobs
              - sagemaker:ListTransformJobs
              - sagemaker:ListProcessingJobs
              - sagemaker:ListAutoMLJobs
              - sagemaker:ListCandidatesForAutoMLJob
              - sagemaker:ListHyperParameterTuningJobs
              - sagemaker:ListTrainingJobsForHyperParameterTuningJob
            Resource: "*"
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: iam:PassRole
            Resource:
              - !Sub "arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/service-role/${AWS::StackName}-${DomainName}-DataScience-Role"
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                iam:PassedToService: sagemaker.amazonaws.com
      Roles:
        - !Ref SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole

  SageMakerExperimentManagementandVizPolicy:
    Type: 'AWS::IAM::Policy'
    Properties:
      PolicyName: 'SageMaker_ExperimentManagementandViz_Policy'
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:AddAssociation'
              - 'sagemaker:CreateAction'
              - 'sagemaker:CreateArtifact'
              - 'sagemaker:CreateContext'
              - 'sagemaker:CreateExperiment'
              - 'sagemaker:CreateTrial'
              - 'sagemaker:CreateTrialComponent'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateAction'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateArtifact'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateContext'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateExperiment'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateTrial'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateTrialComponent'
              - 'sagemaker:AssociateTrialComponent'
              - 'sagemaker:DisassociateTrialComponent'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteAssociation'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteAction'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteArtifact'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteContext'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteExperiment'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteTrial'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteTrialComponent'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeAction'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeArtifact'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeContext'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeExperiment'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeTrial'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeTrialComponent'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeLineageGroup'
            Resource: 'arn:aws:sagemaker:*:*:*/*'
          - Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:ListAssociations'
              - 'sagemaker:ListActions'
              - 'sagemaker:ListArtifacts'
              - 'sagemaker:ListContexts'
              - 'sagemaker:ListExperiments'
              - 'sagemaker:ListTrials'
              - 'sagemaker:ListTrialComponents'
              - 'sagemaker:ListLineageGroups'
              - 'sagemaker:GetLineageGroupPolicy'
              - 'sagemaker:QueryLineage'
              - 'sagemaker:Search'
              - 'sagemaker:GetSearchSuggestions'
            Resource: '*'
      Roles:
        - !Ref SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole

  SageMakerModelManagementPolicy:
    Type: "AWS::IAM::Policy"
    Properties:
      PolicyName: "SageMaker_ModelManagement_Policy"
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Action:
              - "sagemaker:CreateModel"
            Resource:
              - "arn:aws:sagemaker:*:*:*/*"
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Action:
              - "sagemaker:CreateModelPackage"
              - "sagemaker:CreateModelPackageGroup"
              - "sagemaker:DescribeModel"
              - "sagemaker:DescribeModelPackage"
              - "sagemaker:DescribeModelPackageGroup"
              - "sagemaker:BatchDescribeModelPackage"
              - "sagemaker:UpdateModelPackage"
              - "sagemaker:DeleteModel"
              - "sagemaker:DeleteModelPackage"
              - "sagemaker:DeleteModelPackageGroup"
            Resource:
              - "arn:aws:sagemaker:*:*:*/*"
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Action:
              - "sagemaker:ListModels"
              - "sagemaker:ListModelPackages"
              - "sagemaker:ListModelPackageGroups"
            Resource: "*"
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Action: "iam:PassRole"
            Resource:
              - !Sub "arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/service-role/${AWS::StackName}-${DomainName}-DataScience-Role"
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                "iam:PassedToService": "sagemaker.amazonaws.com"
      Roles:
        - !Ref SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole

  SageMakerStudioAppPermissionPolicy:
    Type: 'AWS::IAM::Policy'
    Properties:
      PolicyName: 'SageMaker_StudioAppPermission_Policy'
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: 'SMStudioUserProfileAppPermissionsCreateAndDelete'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:CreateApp'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteApp'
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:app/*'
            Condition:
              'Null':
                sagemaker:OwnerUserProfileArn: 'true'
          - Sid: 'SMStudioCreatePresignedDomainUrlForUserProfile'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:CreatePresignedDomainUrl'
            Resource:
              # - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user-profile/${sagemaker:DomainId}/${sagemaker:UserProfileName}'
              - Fn::Join:
                  - ""
                  - - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user-profile/'
                    - "${sagemaker:DomainId}/${sagemaker:UserProfileName}"
          - Sid: 'SMStudioAppPermissionsListAndDescribe'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:ListApps'
              - 'sagemaker:ListDomains'
              - 'sagemaker:ListUserProfiles'
              - 'sagemaker:ListSpaces'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeApp'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeDomain'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeUserProfile'
              - 'sagemaker:DescribeSpace'
            Resource:
              - '*'
          - Sid: 'SMStudioAppPermissionsTagOnCreate'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:AddTags'
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*/*'
            Condition:
              'Null':
                sagemaker:TaggingAction: 'false'
          - Sid: 'SMStudioRestrictSharedSpacesWithoutOwners'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:CreateSpace'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateSpace'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteSpace'
            Resource:
              # - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:space/${sagemaker:DomainId}/*'
              - Fn::Join:
                  - ""
                  - - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:space/'
                    - "${sagemaker:DomainId}/*"
            Condition:
              'Null':
                sagemaker:OwnerUserProfileArn: 'true'
          - Sid: 'SMStudioRestrictSpacesToOwnerUserProfile'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:CreateSpace'
              - 'sagemaker:UpdateSpace'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteSpace'
            Resource:
              # - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:space/${sagemaker:DomainId}/*'
              - Fn::Join:
                  - ""
                  - - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:space/'
                    - "${sagemaker:DomainId}/*"
            Condition:
              ArnLike:
                sagemaker:OwnerUserProfileArn:
                  # - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user-profile/${sagemaker:DomainId}/${sagemaker:UserProfileName}'
                  - Fn::Join:
                    - ""
                    - - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user-profile/'
                      - "${sagemaker:DomainId}/*"
              StringEquals:
                sagemaker:SpaceSharingType:
                  - 'Private'
                  - 'Shared'
          - Sid: 'SMStudioRestrictCreatePrivateSpaceAppsToOwnerUserProfile'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:CreateApp'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteApp'
            Resource:
              # - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:app/${sagemaker:DomainId}/*'
              - Fn::Join:
                  - ""
                  - - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:app/'
                    - "${sagemaker:DomainId}/*"
            Condition:
              ArnLike:
                sagemaker:OwnerUserProfileArn:
                  # - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user-profile/${sagemaker:DomainId}/${sagemaker:UserProfileName}'
                  - Fn::Join:
                    - ""
                    - - !Sub 'arn:aws:sagemaker:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user-profile/'
                      - "${sagemaker:DomainId}/${sagemaker:UserProfileName}"
              StringEquals:
                sagemaker:SpaceSharingType:
                  - 'Private'
          - Sid: 'AllowAppActionsForSharedSpaces'
            Effect: 'Allow'
            Action:
              - 'sagemaker:CreateApp'
              - 'sagemaker:DeleteApp'
            Resource: 'arn:aws:sagemaker:*:*:app/${sagemaker:DomainId}/*/*/*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                sagemaker:SpaceSharingType:
                  - 'Shared'
      Roles:
        - !Ref SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole

  SageMakerStudioVPCOnlyDomain:
    Type: AWS::SageMaker::Domain
    Properties:
      AppNetworkAccessType: VpcOnly
      AuthMode: IAM
      DomainName: !Ref DomainName
      SubnetIds:
        - !Ref SageMakerSubnet
      VpcId: !Ref SageMakerVpc
      DefaultUserSettings:
        SecurityGroups:
          - !Ref SageMakerSecurityGroup
        ExecutionRole: !GetAtt SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole.Arn

  UserProfile:
    Type: AWS::SageMaker::UserProfile
    Properties:
      DomainId: !Ref SageMakerStudioVPCOnlyDomain
      UserProfileName: !Ref StudioUserName
      UserSettings:
        ExecutionRole: !GetAtt SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole.Arn

Outputs:

  NewSageMakerDomain:
    Description: "New Domain Id"
    Value: !Ref SageMakerStudioVPCOnlyDomain

  NewSageMakerExecutionRole:
    Description: "SageMaker Data Science Role"
    Value: !Ref SageMakerStudioDataScienceRole

  SageMakerDomainUrl:
    Value: !Join
      - ''
      - - 'https://console.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/home?region='
        - !Ref 'AWS::Region'
        - '#/studio/'
        - !Ref SageMakerStudioVPCOnlyDomain
    Description: URL to access the SageMaker Domain

cfn_description: Gateway Stack - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway infrastructure for MCP integration
content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'Gateway Stack - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway infrastructure for MCP integration'

# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE OVERVIEW
# ============================================================================
# This CloudFormation template deploys Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
# with MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for AI agent communication.
#
# Key Components:
# - IAM Role for AgentCore Gateway with Lambda invoke permissions
# - AgentCore Gateway with JWT authorization (Cognito integration)
# - Gateway Target connecting to Lambda function for protein prediction
# - MCP tool schema defining invoke_endpoint and get_results operations
#
# Dependencies:
# - VEP Stack: Requires Lambda function ARN from SSM Parameter Store
# - Cognito Stack: Requires discovery URL and client ID from SSM Parameter Store
#
# Stack Deployment Order:
# 1. VEP Endpoint Stack (creates Lambda, stores ARN in SSM)
# 2. Cognito Stack (creates auth config, stores in SSM)
# 3. Gateway Stack (reads from SSM, creates gateway) <- THIS STACK
#
# Outputs:
# - Gateway URL for MCP client connections
# - Gateway ID and ARN for reference
# - IAM role information
# ============================================================================

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: 'Project Configuration'
        Parameters:
          - ProjectName
      - Label:
          default: 'Gateway Configuration'
        Parameters:
          - GatewayName
          - GatewayDescription
    ParameterLabels:
      ProjectName:
        default: 'Project Name'
      GatewayName:
        default: 'Gateway Name'
      GatewayDescription:
        default: 'Gateway Description'

# ============================================================================
# PARAMETERS
# ============================================================================
# Configure Gateway naming and description
# ============================================================================

Parameters:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Project Configuration
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ProjectName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'protein-engineering'
    Description: 'Project name used for resource naming and tagging'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens'

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gateway Configuration
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GatewayName:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: 'Name for the AgentCore Gateway (leave empty to auto-generate from project name)'
    MaxLength: 128
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores'

  GatewayDescription:
    Type: String
    Default: 'AgentCore Gateway for protein engineering agent with MCP integration'
    Description: 'Description for the AgentCore Gateway'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 256

# ============================================================================
# CONDITIONS
# ============================================================================
Conditions:
  UseGeneratedGatewayName: !Equals [!Ref GatewayName, '']

# ============================================================================
# RESOURCES
# ============================================================================
Resources:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PLACEHOLDER VALUES (was a self-containment gap on a separate VEP Endpoint
  # stack and Cognito stack, see TEMPLATE OVERVIEW above). First fix stubbed
  # these via AWS::SSM::Parameter + {{resolve:ssm:...}} dynamic references,
  # but that failed on real AWS with a stack-level "no StackStatusReason or
  # FAILED resource event found" error: CloudFormation resolves dynamic
  # references during an early template-processing pass that does not
  # reliably honor DependsOn against a parameter created earlier in the SAME
  # template (confirmed via CloudTrail -- the stack failed before the SSM
  # ssm:PutParameter call for these resources ever happened). Since these
  # were only ever placeholder/non-secret values anyway, inlined them as
  # plain literals instead -- no dynamic reference, no ordering hazard.
  #
  # The Lambda ARN placeholder can stay a plain string (it's just an IAM
  # policy Resource/GatewayTarget property, never independently validated).
  # The Cognito discovery URL could NOT stay a fake string, though: AgentCore
  # Gateway creation actually HTTP-fetches AuthorizerConfiguration's
  # DiscoveryUrl to build the JWT authorizer, so a placeholder domain fails
  # with "Failed to fetch discovery document" (confirmed on a real deploy
  # attempt). Fixed by creating a real (empty, unused) Cognito User Pool +
  # Client below -- every real User Pool automatically serves a working OIDC
  # discovery document at this well-known path, no Domain/UI needed for that.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PlaceholderUserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway-placeholder-pool'

  PlaceholderUserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway-placeholder-client'
      UserPoolId: !Ref PlaceholderUserPool
      GenerateSecret: false

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM ROLE FOR AGENTCORE GATEWAY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Allows Gateway to invoke Lambda function for protein prediction
  # Uses dynamic SSM reference to get Lambda ARN from VEP stack
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GatewayRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    # Purpose: Grants AgentCore Gateway permission to invoke Lambda function
    # Trust Policy: Only bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com can assume this role
    # Conditions: Restricts to same account and AgentCore service ARNs
    # Permissions: lambda:InvokeFunction on the placeholder Lambda ARN below
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-agentcore-gateway-role'
      Description: 'Execution role for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to invoke Lambda functions'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref AWS::AccountId
              ArnLike:
                'aws:SourceArn': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:bedrock-agentcore:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: 'LambdaInvokeAccess'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:lambda:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:function:protein-agent-placeholder'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: Component
          Value: Gateway
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM PARAMETER FOR GATEWAY ROLE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stores Gateway role ARN for reference (optional, for future use)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GatewayRoleArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    # Purpose: Stores Gateway IAM role ARN for reference
    # Usage: Can be used by monitoring or management tools
    Properties:
      Name: '/protein-agent/gateway/role-arn'
      Description: 'AgentCore Gateway IAM role ARN'
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt GatewayRole.Arn
      Tier: Standard
      Tags:
        Project: !Ref ProjectName
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AGENTCORE GATEWAY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Main gateway resource that provides MCP endpoint for AI agents
  # Configured with JWT authorization using Cognito
  # Uses dynamic SSM references to retrieve Cognito configuration
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AgentCoreGateway:
    Type: AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Gateway
    # Purpose: Creates MCP-compatible gateway for AI agent communication
    # Protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol) with SEMANTIC search
    # Authorization: CUSTOM_JWT using Cognito for token validation
    Properties:
      Name: !If [UseGeneratedGatewayName, !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway', !Ref GatewayName]
      Description: !Ref GatewayDescription
      RoleArn: !GetAtt GatewayRole.Arn
      ProtocolType: MCP
      AuthorizerType: CUSTOM_JWT
      AuthorizerConfiguration:
        CustomJWTAuthorizer:
          DiscoveryUrl: !Sub 'https://cognito-idp.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${PlaceholderUserPool}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
          AllowedClients:
            - !Ref PlaceholderUserPoolClient
      ProtocolConfiguration:
        Mcp:
          SearchType: SEMANTIC
      Tags:
        Project: !Ref ProjectName
        Component: Gateway
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # GATEWAY TARGET
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Connects Gateway to Lambda function with MCP tool schema
  # Defines invoke_endpoint and get_results operations
  # Uses dynamic SSM reference to retrieve Lambda ARN from VEP stack
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GatewayTarget:
    Type: AWS::BedrockAgentCore::GatewayTarget
    # Purpose: Connects Gateway to Lambda function for protein prediction
    # Tool Schema: Defines two MCP tools (invoke_endpoint, get_results)
    # Credentials: Uses Gateway IAM role for Lambda invocation
    Properties:
      Name: 'protein-engineering-lambda'
      Description: 'Lambda target for protein variant effect prediction'
      GatewayIdentifier: !Ref AgentCoreGateway
      TargetConfiguration:
        Mcp:
          Lambda:
            LambdaArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:lambda:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:function:protein-agent-placeholder'
            ToolSchema:
              InlinePayload:
                - Name: 'invoke_endpoint'
                  Description: 'Submit a job to predict the variant effects for an amino acid sequence'
                  InputSchema:
                    Type: 'object'
                    Properties:
                      sequence:
                        Type: 'string'
                        Description: 'Amino acid sequence'
                    Required:
                      - 'sequence'
                - Name: 'get_results'
                  Description: 'Check if a variant effect prediction job has completed and retrieve results'
                  InputSchema:
                    Type: 'object'
                    Properties:
                      output_id:
                        Type: 'string'
                        Description: 'output_id returned by invoke_endpoint'
                    Required:
                      - 'output_id'
      CredentialProviderConfigurations:
        - CredentialProviderType: GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE

# ============================================================================
# OUTPUTS
# ============================================================================
# Provides Gateway connection information and resource identifiers
# ============================================================================

Outputs:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gateway Outputs
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GatewayId:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway ID'
    Value: !Ref AgentCoreGateway
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayId'

  GatewayUrl:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway MCP URL'
    Value: !GetAtt AgentCoreGateway.GatewayUrl
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayUrl'

  GatewayArn:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway ARN'
    Value: !GetAtt AgentCoreGateway.GatewayArn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayArn'

  # IAM Role Outputs
  GatewayRoleArn:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway IAM role ARN'
    Value: !GetAtt GatewayRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayRoleArn'

  GatewayRoleName:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway IAM role name'
    Value: !Ref GatewayRole
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayRoleName'

  # Target Outputs
  TargetId:
    Description: 'Gateway Target ID'
    Value: !Ref GatewayTarget
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TargetId'

  TargetName:
    Description: 'Gateway Target name'
    Value: 'protein-engineering-lambda'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TargetName'

  # SSM Parameter Outputs
  GatewayRoleArnParameterName:
    Description: 'SSM Parameter name for Gateway role ARN'
    Value: '/protein-agent/gateway/role-arn'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayRoleArnParameter'

  # Configuration Outputs
  ProjectName:
    Description: 'Project name used for resource naming'
    Value: !Ref ProjectName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ProjectName'

  GatewayName:
    Description: 'Gateway name'
    Value: !If [UseGeneratedGatewayName, !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway', !Ref GatewayName]
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayName'

resource_types: AWS::EC2::EIP | AWS::EC2::InternetGateway | AWS::EC2::NatGateway | AWS::EC2::Route | AWS::EC2::RouteTable | AWS::EC2::Subnet | AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation | AWS::EC2::VPC | AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment

The template creates a VPC, public and private subnets
